title: Boost performance of Go applications with profile guided optimization
description: By profiling Go applications at runtime, the Go compiler can make better optimization decisions in subsequent builds, leading to substantial improvements in CPU performance. In this technical session, developers will learn how profile-guided optimization works and how they can use it to improve (and measure) their application performance on Google Cloud and beyond. Profile-guided optimization blog post https://goo.gle/go-blog-pgo Profile-guided optimization documentation https://goo.gle/go-doc-pgo Profiling Go applications with Google Cloud Profiler https://goo.gle/3Qjt45I

segments.heading: System Capabilities, Implementation Details, and Workload Optimization
segments.text: As Cameron mentioned earlier, my name is Michael. I'm a software engineer on the Go team at Google. I'm going to dive into Profile Guided Optimization, which was added to Go in Go 121 last year. Profile Guided Optimization, or PGO, is a category of compiler optimization techniques supported by a variety of different languages. With PGO, the compiler's using information about the runtime behavior of an application in order to improve the optimization decisions made during compilation. Now, you may have also heard the term Feedback Directed Optimization, or FDO, FDO and PGO are just interchangeable terms for the exact same concepts.
